methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: A Norfolk native delivering free AI workshops directly addresses the distribution challenge in a non-hub region, signaling peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could build grassroots fluency outside traditional tech centers.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Animatronics, AI and more at Virginia Tech’s Music + Technology Festival
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's specialized AI+music festival and Roanoke College's Google partnership show institutional depth in mid-tier regions, but free training certificates suggest shallow platform-mediated adoption rather than indigenous capability building.

signals.title: 3 principles to make AI data centers good grid citizens - Utility Dive
signals.signal_reading: NoVA leaders debating data center impacts reveals infrastructure concentration without corresponding human capability distribution—physical AI assets clustering while community concerns suggest limited local workforce integration or benefit sharing.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools adopting ChatGPT under division oversight signals platform-layer AI diffusion reaching K-12, but institutional gatekeeping approach suggests managed, shallow integration rather than deep computational literacy development.

signals.title: VA Plans New AI Tools to Cut Administrative Burden - MeriTalk
signals.signal_reading: VA's administrative AI tools represent government-wide shallow adoption through vendor platforms—distributing efficiency gains but not building internal technical capacity or transferable AI fluency across Virginia's workforce.
